sentences.text:
The instant appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 challenges the judgment and award dated 10.01.2013 passed in M.A.C.P. No.412 of 2011 by the Motor Accident Claim Tribunal,
Sabarkantha at Himatnagar.

entities.text:
Motor Accident Claim Tribunal,
Sabarkantha at Himatnagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The brief facts of the case are as under.

2.1 On 24.04.2011, applicant of MACP No.411 of 2011 along with her two children were standing on eastern side of road from Ilol Cross road, at that time, at about 5.15 pm, driver of Car No.GJ-9-AG-7191 came driving his vehicle in rash and negligent manner and dashed applicant of MACP No.411 of 2011 and minor Soban, applicant of MACP No.412 of 2011 and as a result of which,
the claimants received injuries.
Therefore, claimants filed claim petition for compensation.

2.2 FIR of incident was registered before the concerned Police Station.
2.3. The claimant filed claim petition under section 166 of MV Act being MACP No.412 of 2011 claiming compensation of Rs.4,00,000/- along with interest jointly and severally from the opponents.
2.4. After appreciating evidence on record, learned Tribunal was pleased to pass judgment and award in tune of Rs.2,86,081/- with 8% interest from the date of claim petition.
2.5. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with impugned judgment and award dated 10.01.2013, the original claimant has filed present appeal.
3. Learned advocate for the appellant submits on the date of accident, son of claimant was minor.
It is submitted that learned Tribunal committed serious error in granting meager amount in case where minor has sustained injury to the extent of 62% body as whole.
Therefore, he submits to intercept the impugned award and enhance the same.
4. On the other hand, learned advocate for the Insurance Company totally supports the judgment and award delivered by the learned Tribunal and submits to pass necessary orders.

5. Having heard learned advocates for both sides, at this juncture, let refer judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Master Mallikarjun V/s. Divisional Manager, National Insurance NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/788/2013 ORDER DATED: 10/12/2024 undefined Company Limited and Anr.,
rendered in Civil Appeal No.7139 of 2013, wherein, the Hon'ble Apex Court held as under:-
""12.

entities.text: Master Mallikarjun V/s. Divisional Manager, National Insurance NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/788/2013
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Though it is difficult to have an accurate assessment of the compensation in the case of children suffering disability on account of a motor vehicle accident, having regard to the relevant factors, precedents and the approach of various High Courts,
we are of the view that the appropriate compensation on all other heads in addition to the actual expenditure for treatment, attendant, etc., should be, if the disability is above 10% and up-to 30% to the whole body, Rs.3 lakhs; upto 60%, Rs.4 lakhs; upto 90%, Rs.5 lakhs and above 90%, it should be Rs.6 lakhs.

For permanent disability upto 10%, it should be Re.1 lakh, unless there are exceptional take different yardstick..."
6.
Apt to note that the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 is a beneficial piece of Legislation.
The concept of just and fair compensation is integral and seminal to the MV Act.

The compensation to be awarded under the principle of just and fair compensation to the injured of the road accident or the legal representative/s of the deceased person is based on the principle of fairness, reasonableness and equability.

Anguish of the heart or for mental turbulence being consequential result of the road accident cannot be actually compensated, but the quint essentiality lies in adopting holistic and pragmatic view to the computation of the compensation for the loss sustained, which is to be in the realm of realistic approximation.

Although exact or perfect arithmetical calculation of compensation Sobanbhai Mohamedshafi Memon- Minor ... vs Sureshbhai Lalbhai Nanavati on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90432325/
2 for reparation of the loss arrived from the road accident is almost impossible.

sentences.text: The Tribunal is bestowed with duty to make an endevour to award just compensation regardless of the amount claimed by the claimants.

The determination of the quantum of compensation NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/788/2013 ORDER DATED: 10/12/2024 undefined therefore, must be liberal and not niggardly since the law values life and limb in a free country in generous scale.

Needless to state that money may be awarded, so that something tangible may be procured to reach something else of the like nature, which has been destroyed or lost, but money cannot renew physical frame that has been battered and shattered being a result of the road accident. Yet Tribunal to endavour to bring back victim to stage of pre-road accident as far as possible Thus, the award must be reasonable and cannot be assessed with moderation though it cannot at the same time be pity and what could be granted must be just, fair and equitable compensation.
7. In the instant case, as per medical certificate, minor claimant has suffered disability to the tune of 62%.
Thus in view of judgment of Mallikarjun (supra), the appellant / claimant would be entitled to get Rs.3,00,000/- as compensation for injury, he has suffered.
In addition, thereto, he would be entitled to compensation under different heads.
Thus, the appellant / claimant would be entitled to get compensation as per following table.

8. Therefore, total compensation would be as under, which the claimant/s is/are entitled to get.
 Particulars   Loss of earning to parents during period of   hospitalization.

C/FA/788/2013 ORDER DATED:
 
 Medical expenses   Special diet, transportation and attendant   charges.

Mental pain, shock and suffering as per   judgment of Mallikarjun (supra)
 Total... 
 Less : Amount which is already awarded   Additional amount which is awarded  Sobanbhai Mohamedshafi Memon- Minor ... vs Sureshbhai Lalbhai Nanavati on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90432325/
3 9.

Therefore, I hold that the claimant is entitled to get the enhanced compensation of Rs.2,49,250/-
with 8% p.a. interest from the date of filing the claim petition till its realisation, which would meet the ends of justice.
Rest of the direction(s) of the Tribunal remain same.
10. For the reasons recorded above, the following order is passed.
10.1 The present appeal is partly allowed.

The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the enhanced amount of Rs.2,49,250/- with 8% p.a. interest from the date of claim petition till its realization before the concerned Tribunal, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of this order.

10.2 The Tribunal shall disburse the entire awarded amount lying in the FDR and/or with the Tribunal, with accrued interest thereon, if any, to the claimant, by account payee cheque / NEFT /
RTGS, after proper verification and after following due procedure.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/788/2013 ORDER DATED: 10/12/2024 undefined 10.3
While making the payment, the Tribunal shall deduct the courts fees, if not paid, in accordance with rules/law.
10.4 Record and proceedings be sent back to the concerned Tribunal, forthwith.
